questions.element: all 16 captured routes, first viewport at 1440 and 390
questions.evidence: all 16 labels x light/dark x 1440/390; leads frontier--light--1440.png, home--light--390.png
questions.note: No route fails: each leads with a small-caps eyebrow, a serif H1 at a weight no other element on the page uses, and a lede at prose measure, and that block survives 390 intact. Home alone has no H1 by design (no hero); its purpose reads from the 'WHAT CHANGED' eyebrow on the feed.

questions.element: / - changed feed (left) and THE FRONTIER door (rail top)
questions.note: The feed still holds the first viewport at 1440 with no hero and is untouched by the door, the rail's first block: three org/model pairs plus 'The whole board - every organisation this site tracks, one row each'. At 390 the rail folds after the whole feed, so the door sits ~2,400px in - a cost of R6, not displacement.

F-K12 holds at both viewports: the reader meets 'AI winter', its kicker and five paragraphs before the FACTS fragment, where the port put FACTS in a right column level with the first line. The record without prose is coherent facts-first.

On all four /tutorials rows at 1440 in both themes the verification date and the word 'verified' paint on top of each other and an orphan separator drops to its own line, so the value discriminating between tutorials is illegible at desktop; at 390 it stacks correctly. Every other index lands the eye on its discriminating value.

Each class matches R8's own test in the pixels: the board (16 rows x 6 columns, values tracked across) and the catalog table carry the rule, the ragged-height home feed carries it, the near-uniform single-line link indexes carry none. The board's rules did not spread to /wiki or /tools.

questions.evidence: frontier--light--1440.png, frontier--dark--1440.png, wiki-entry--light--1440.png vs port wiki-entry--light--1440.png
questions.note: At 1440 the board's last column is cut mid-word on all 16 rows ('Qwen, launched in beta April 2023 as Ton') with no affordance saying more exists, so the widest viewport shows an unreadable column; at 390 it honestly clips to two columns. Retiring the wiki entry's second column also left the right half of the 1440 viewport empty, growing the same content 2349 to 2950px.

questions.element: #frontier vendor-claim cell, CLAIMED - UNVERIFIED chip, 16/16 rows
questions.note: Relocation, exactly: the hatch was demoted as asked (0 of 16 rows blank, so none renders), but a bordered 'CLAIMED - UNVERIFIED' chip now repeats on every row - the default state drawn as a chip, R8's badge clause verbatim, and the loudest non-discriminating mark on the flagship. /catalog prints ACTIVE plain; /wiki chips only exceptions.

questions.element: self-check against the contract's evidence table
questions.note: Every verdict comes from a PNG in the declared class at 1440 and 390 in both themes; no hover, focus, motion or scroll state was judged, and document order was read only from fullPage captures where it is in frame. The one property I could not see - /catalog at 390 - is an evidence-fix.

findings.problem: The vendor-claim cell renders a bordered 'CLAIMED - UNVERIFIED' chip on 16 of 16 rows, so the default state is a chip on every row and the flagship's loudest repeated mark - R8's badge clause, and round-1's critical relocated into a border.
findings.invariant: On /frontier a bordered chip renders only on rows whose vendor-claim state differs from the state most rows carry; a state shared by all rows renders as unbordered muted text.
findings.prescription: Print the claim state the way /catalog prints ACTIVE - plain, muted, unbordered - keeping the chip for a verified or disputed row.

findings.problem: At 1440 the VENDOR CLAIM column is truncated mid-word on all 16 rows at the board container's right edge, with no rule, fade or scroll affordance in frame saying content continues.
findings.invariant: At 1440 no board cell's text is clipped by its container: a column that cannot fit is dropped whole (the packet's own index-position rule) or ellipsised in the cell.
findings.prescription: Clamp the cell to one ellipsised line and let the model record carry the sentence, or drop the column at 1440 as the index column was dropped.

findings.problem: Retiring the wiki entry's second column satisfied F-K12 but left the right half of the 1440 viewport empty and grew the same entry 2349 to 2950px, so the prose template carries less per screen than the port.
findings.invariant: On /wiki/<entry> at 1440 prose still precedes facts (S14) AND the content occupies a stated share of the shell, not one measure-wide column against empty space.
findings.prescription: Use the R13 round-1 rail track for the entry's marks and dates, or set the facts fragment two-up below the prose.

findings.problem: On /tutorials at 1440 in both themes the verification date and the word 'verified' overprint each other on every row and the separator orphans onto its own line, making the index's discriminating value illegible.
findings.invariant: On /tutorials at 1440 the row metadata line renders date and label as separate, non-overlapping runs on one baseline.
findings.prescription: None asserted - inherited from the port, not caused by the delta; filed so the finalist is not signed off carrying it.

findings.problem: The packet's headline catalog change (two dense lines per row below 34rem) cannot be judged: table-catalog--*--390.png is a 4.4 MB, 48,520px fullPage of all 431 rows - the inverse of the L5 case the rig handles at 1440.
findings.invariant: A route captured as 'viewport' at one viewport is captured as 'viewport' at every viewport in the coverage line, so its first-screen density is judgeable at 390.
findings.prescription: Re-capture /catalog at 390 as a viewport capture, or cap fullPage height and label the entry.

findings.problem: At 390 the Frontier door is the rail's first block, but the rail folds after the whole changed feed, so the flagship sits ~2,400px into the home document.
findings.invariant: At 390 a link to /frontier is reachable from the home first viewport (the nav counts) without traversing the feed.
findings.prescription: None beyond the existing nav item; keeper decides whether K19 binds home at 390 or only the route.

carried_forward.note: Hatch demoted; moot because 0 of 16 rows render blank. The defect it named relocated into the chip - see F-hier-5.
Built as a fixed two-column excerpt citing R6 and R2; my invariant is met in home--light--390.png. Not re-filed.
Never declared per surface, but the board's rules did not reach /wiki, /tools or /data and each class matches R8's test.
ORGANISATION and CURRENT MODEL are the one 700-weight underlined column pair, giving the board a first-read entry point.

diagnosis.strongest: HIER - the first-read block (eyebrow, one dominant serif H1, lede) is consistent across all 16 routes at both viewports, F-K12 is satisfied on the entry the keeper complained about, F-hier-4 gave the board its entry point, and R8 classes are correct.
diagnosis.weakest: DENS on the flagship - /frontier is at once too loud (a default-state chip on 16 of 16 rows) and too quiet (its last column truncated mid-word at 1440), and the wiki entry's F-K12 fix bought correct order at the price of half an empty viewport.
diagnosis.critical_issue: Round-1's critical was not resolved, it moved: the hatch was demoted as asked, and the flagship's repeated non-discriminating mark is now a bordered CLAIMED - UNVERIFIED chip on every row - the same forbidden shape in a new channel, on a surface where /catalog and /wiki in the same build do it correctly.
diagnosis.highest_value_improvement: Fix the board's last column: clamp the vendor-claim cell to one ellipsised line and print its state as plain muted text, not a chip. One change removes the flagship's loudest non-discriminating mark and stops a column being cut mid-word at the widest viewport.

downstream.weakness: The board is a good hierarchy carrying two chrome defects in one cell - the vendor-claim column is at once the loudest thing on the page and the only unreadable one.
downstream.cause: That cell holds a prose sentence inside a tabular grid, so it needed a badge to look like a cell and more width than a cell has; the honest-blank premise never fired, since 16 of 16 orgs matched a provider.
downstream.recommendation: Rebuild the cell as a short state word plus a link into the model record, and re-capture /catalog at 390 as a viewport capture before the next panel.
